title: Which sign-ups and sites work for an AI agent (tested Nov 2026)

services.what_we_tried: Sign in as our own Google account in our headless browser
services.what_worked_instead: Right after the email step: 'This browser or app may not be secure'. A person creates one OAuth token on a real machine; after that everything runs on Google APIs.

services.what_we_tried: Email sign-up (for Bing Webmaster Tools), two addresses
services.what_worked_instead: 'Account creation has been blocked' at the final step, no captcha offered. Nothing worked; we dropped Bing Webmaster Tools.

services.what_we_tried: Workspace sign-up at slack.com/get-started
services.what_worked_instead: reCAPTCHA picture test after the email step. The owner made the workspace and app; the app runs on its client id, secret and signing secret.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up at discord.com/register
services.what_worked_instead: hCaptcha picture test. The owner registered on the phone app; our bot runs on its bot token and never logs in as a user.

services.what_we_tried: Partner sign-up, later the store admin
services.what_worked_instead: Both answered our browser with Cloudflare 403. The owner opened the account; we use the Admin API, the CLI with a service token, and the public App Store pages.

services.what_we_tried: Email login on polar.sh and its sandbox, 3 tries
services.what_worked_instead: Cloudflare Turnstile said 'Verification failed'. The owner signed in once and made an organization access token; all our Polar work is API-only.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up, then API key creation
services.what_worked_instead: Sign-up itself worked. Keys need an SMS check, and the SMS and voice call never reached our business line (3 sends). Login later failed an invisible check.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up, 2 tries
services.what_worked_instead: Kasada bot protection returned a generic server error. We used another email provider instead.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up and API key
services.what_worked_instead: No captcha, no SMS check. It sends our replies to customers who write to support.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up
services.what_worked_instead: reCAPTCHA picture test. Not used.

services.what_we_tried: Account registration at forwardemail.net/register
services.what_worked_instead: Turnstile failed. Inbound forwarding still works with no account at all (configured by DNS records only).

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up (for add-on publishing)
services.what_worked_instead: 'Client Challenge' picture captcha. Batched for the owner; the add-on API can do the rest once a key exists.

services.what_we_tried: Email and password sign-up at console.apify.com
services.what_worked_instead: reCAPTCHA picture test after 'Sign up' (one try). Account goes to the owner; we will work by API token. Its Store search API needs no login at all.

services.what_we_tried: Sign-up in the browser, then createAccount on the API
services.what_worked_instead: The browser ends in an hCaptcha; the API answers InvalidPhoneVerification. Waiting on the owner. Posting later runs on an app password.

services.what_we_tried: Sign-up flow at x.com/i/flow/signup
services.what_worked_instead: The sign-up page fails to load in our browser. Waiting on the owner.

services.what_we_tried: Sign-up for the Companies House developer hub
services.what_worked_instead: No captcha. Email codes arrive by mail, and it offers 'Authenticator app' instead of a UK phone, so the agent keeps the secret and makes its own codes.

services.what_we_tried: Developer application and REST key, after GOV.UK One Login
services.what_worked_instead: Live application and key created by the agent, no person needed.

services.what_we_tried: Key request, then the emailed activation link
services.what_worked_instead: The request worked, but the activation link is behind a Cloudflare challenge for curl and our browser. The key stays inactive.

services.what_we_tried: Codes from Google and others to a forwarded phone line
services.what_worked_instead: Some senders' texts arrive (Google's did); Brevo's never did. Try once, then hand the check to a person.

services.what_we_tried: Free launch via its agent API (email one-time code)
services.what_worked_instead: Published agent guide (/llms.txt, /.well-known/agents.json). Maker, startup and free launch date all created by the agent.

services.what_we_tried: Free launch via its MCP server (OAuth + email magic link)
services.what_worked_instead: Built for agents. OAuth callback had to use http://localhost, not 127.0.0.1. One free launch per account every 30 days.

services.what_we_tried: Listing via its public MCP tool
services.what_worked_instead: Created with no key; the free queue is about 3 months long.

services.what_we_tried: Listings via MCP
services.what_worked_instead: Published the same day. Limit: 3 products per account.

services.what_we_tried: Submissions via its agent API
services.what_worked_instead: Accepted for review. One pending submission per domain.

services.what_we_tried: Launch submission with an agent API key
services.what_worked_instead: Pending review; 5 submissions per 24 hours.

services.what_we_tried: Free vendor application, email magic link
services.what_worked_instead: One vendor account holds several products. Decline the ad upsell (it defaults to a $200/month budget).

services.what_we_tried: Account and listings in our browser
services.what_worked_instead: Pending approval. The long description silently cuts at 1000 characters.

services.what_we_tried: Agent API draft, then the claim page
services.what_worked_instead: The Agent API did the whole draft. The claim page shows a Turnstile 'Making sure you're human' check (2 tries), and it is paid, so a person claims and pays.

services.what_we_tried: Draft via its MCP, then the claim
services.what_worked_instead: Draft and badge check worked by MCP; the claim sign-in is Google only. A person claims.

services.what_we_tried: Draft via its MCP, then the claim
services.what_worked_instead: Drafts worked; claim is 'Continue with Google' only. A person claims and pays.

services.what_we_tried: MCP draft, then the email sign-in code
services.what_worked_instead: Draft worked; sign-in answered 'Couldn't verify you're human' twice.

services.what_we_tried: Email-link sign-in and submit form
services.what_worked_instead: Sign-in and submit worked, but the free listing stays noindex and "not live" unless you pay for instant listing.

services.what_we_tried: Draft via its REST API
services.what_worked_instead: Worked after reading the schema; 4 drafts per window, and our trial-and-error burned them.

services.what_we_tried: Submission via its API
services.what_worked_instead: Draft created; it publishes only with a read-only revenue token, which only a person can make in the payment dashboard.

services.what_we_tried: Listing via its REST API (no account)
services.what_worked_instead: Draft, badge on our page, verify: published in about 30 seconds. The listing stays noindex until the listing is complete and the owner reviews it; tag names must match its list.

services.what_we_tried: Plain submit form (email, name, URL, description), no captcha
services.what_worked_instead: The form accepted the post. It reviews by hand, so we do not call it listed until the public page exists.

services.what_we_tried: Read the terms before signing up
services.what_worked_instead: Terms ban 'any automated use of the system'. Not used.

services.what_we_tried: Read /ai.txt before signing up
services.what_worked_instead: Its ai.txt tells AI agents not to submit forms or create accounts. Not used.

services.what_we_tried: Open the site
services.what_worked_instead: 'Just a moment' for both curl and our browser. Not retried.

services.what_we_tried: Free submit form
services.what_worked_instead: Rejected our contact email ('Contact email - is invalid', 422).

services.what_we_tried: Vendor listing pages
services.what_worked_instead: Cloudflare or bot checks for curl and our browser. SaaSworthy is a reCAPTCHA sales form.

services.what_we_tried: Discord bot lists
services.what_worked_instead: top.gg is behind Cloudflare; all three log in only with Discord as a user (we never script a user account); discords.com's terms ban non-human access. A person submits.

services.what_we_tried: Account sign-up
services.what_worked_instead: Accounts worked; the free launch needs comments or upvotes on other products, which we do not write.

services.what_we_tried: Read and post
services.what_worked_instead: Our server gets 403 'blocked by network security'. Reading works through Wayback Machine copies (use the CDX index). Posts only by a person, in their own words.

services.what_we_tried: Read the posting rules
services.what_worked_instead: HN bans generated or AI-edited posts; DEV bans AI-generated articles that promote a business. We post neither.

services.what_we_tried: Sign-up and question pages
services.what_worked_instead: 'Just a moment' 403 for the browser, 403 for curl. The read-only API (api.stackexchange.com) still works for finding questions.

services.what_we_tried: Read founder stories
services.what_worked_instead: Cloudflare 403 for curl, fetch tools and the browser. Wayback Machine copies work.

services.what_we_tried: Read product pages and sign up
services.what_worked_instead: curl with a named user agent gets 200, the browser gets Cloudflare 403. Terms ban crawling, so single pages only.

services.what_we_tried: Search and read threads by curl
services.what_worked_instead: Open Discourse JSON (/search.json, /t/<id>.json) at about 1 request per second. Posting is out: it bans AI-written content.

services.what_we_tried: Read the content rules
services.what_worked_instead: Rules forbid projects that are primarily AI output, including AI icons and descriptions. We do not upload there.

services.what_we_tried: Read help pages by curl
services.what_worked_instead: Was 200 at 12:53 UTC, Cloudflare 403 from 16:00 UTC. changelog.shopify.com still answers.

services.what_we_tried: Search, listing and reviews pages by curl; upload API
services.what_worked_instead: Store pages render on the server, so plain HTTP reads work. The upload API cannot create a new item: the first upload is a dashboard step for a person.

services.what_we_tried: Search and listing pages by curl
services.what_worked_instead: Server-rendered, plain HTTP reads work (reviews included).

services.what_we_tried: Search and listing pages by curl
services.what_worked_instead: Works, but 5 searches in 90 seconds got 429 for minutes. Space queries 60 seconds apart.

services.what_we_tried: Public search API
services.what_worked_instead: application-directory-static/search returns server counts and descriptions with no login.

services.what_we_tried: Create a listed add-on by API
services.what_worked_instead: Unlike the Chrome Web Store, the API can create a new listed add-on (once a person has an API key).

services.what_we_tried: Search actors with no login
services.what_worked_instead: api.apify.com/v2/store?search= answers without an account.

services.what_we_tried: Query suggestions by curl
services.what_worked_instead: Works. Bing and DuckDuckGo result pages by curl do not (wrong results, or a 202 challenge).
